prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a parking lot collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1245; do not mention it.)
text:
This firm represents the individual injured in a collision that occurred in a parking lot and involving a vehicle insured under your policy. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, email, or in person. If your insured or any representative has already made contact with our client, please inform us in writing of the nature of that contact.

We request that you confirm in writing the bodily injury and property damage liability limits of the policy in force at the time of the incident, together with the identity of any excess or umbrella coverage that may apply. Please also provide the claim number assigned to this matter.

We further demand that your company, its insureds, and its agents preserve all evidence relating to this incident. This includes photographs, dash camera or surveillance footage, telematics and vehicle data, recorded statements, claim file materials, adjuster notes, and any maintenance or repair records for the vehicles involved. Failure to preserve such evidence may result in serious consequences in any resulting litigation. We look forward to your prompt written response.
